openings.claim: Update behind-desk exceptions whenever books move; record household-name discrepancies.
openings.discriminator: Verified addresses reduce second searches; persistent burst delays favor queue congestion.
openings.probe: Record address correctness, second searches, queue presence, and preparation/reconciliation time during a capped trial.
openings.uncertainty: Update feasibility and whether household mismatches cause second searches remain unknown.

openings.claim: A bounded arrival cohort might be retrieved faster from the cart; shelving is not universally faster.
openings.discriminator: Matched cart advantage supports retention; disappearance with volume/size favors sample selection.
openings.probe: Observe comparable natural cart/shelf pickups, recording arrival volume and book size.
openings.uncertainty: Capacity, comparable cohorts, and routine retention remain unproven; unmatched comparisons are inconclusive.

openings.claim: Locator instability may dominate delay, including misleading household surnames and stale exceptions.
openings.discriminator: Accurate shelf/cart times converge; inaccurate cues concentrate long searches.
openings.probe: Record first cue, actual location, candidate count, rush status, and retrieval time; stop annotation at the cap.
openings.uncertainty: Dominance is hypothesized; comparable cases may be unavailable.

openings.claim: Physical shelf interference may dominate independently of locator accuracy.
openings.discriminator: Accurate shelf pickups remain slower than matched cart pickups; convergence defeats this explanation.
openings.probe: Use D3's identical observational probe and stopping rule.
openings.uncertainty: Visibility is hypothetical; book size and arrival recency may confound comparisons.

decision: Compare explanations before selecting an intervention. Fits cover bounded probes only: sole existing clerk; names/contact details behind desk; existing two shelves/cart; all added preparation/corrections within ten clerk-minutes. Verify claimant-to-hold before handoff, although the procedure is unspecified. Synthetic evidence establishes neither benefit nor 95% pickups within two minutes/zero wrong-reader handoffs. Reader presence concerns and interview representativeness remain unresolved.
